channel.title: Echo's Reading Feed
channel.description: Curated reading lists: how live events and esports get made. Items marked [recommended] are the picks.

item.title: [recommended] Electric Zoo Part 3 - Load Out
item.description: Kelly Levstek (SoundGirls) - A storm-canceled festival turns into a muddy overnight strike, with too few hands, tangled cables and several departments trying to pack at once.

item.title: [recommended] A gaming event in a League of its own
item.description: Tristan Greaves (Tech Interrupt) - Backstage tour of the Worlds 2024 final at the O2 in London: 72 cameras, 80 transmission lines, 256 audio channels, 1,500+ on-site crew. Shows the scale from the floor, not the control room.

item.title: [recommended] Riot Games streamlines production of Valorant Champions Paris with ST 2110 flypack
item.description: SVG Europe - Riot's new IP-based flypack: tech load-in cut from two days to about four hours, around 40 feeds out to language partners, 80ms round trip to Dublin. Explains why crews are changing.

item.title: [recommended] Tech-eye view: Inside the epic remote production for LoL Worlds Finals 2024
item.description: SVG Europe - Q&A with Riot's broadcast engineering manager. What stays on site (truck, co-streamers) versus what runs from Riot's Dublin remote broadcast center, plus the automated vertical feed.

item.title: [recommended] League of Legends' unsung heroes: The magician of MSI 2023
item.description: PCGamesN - Interview with Sebastian Leathlean, stage manager for every League international event since 2017. What a stage manager does for teams and players on the day.

item.title: [recommended] Touring 101 - Life on The Road pt.1
item.description: Chris Shrom - A lighting professional explains club, theatre, arena, stadium and fly-date life, including trucks, bus calls and corporate-show waiting.

item.title: TrustFall Technology Group Transforms Las Vegas Convention Center Into Evo 2026 Esports Arena in Less Than 72 Hours
item.description: Aroluxe / TrustFall (EIN Presswire) - The Evo 2026 company release describes roughly 300 crew, a three-day build, LED walls, rigging points and the audio problem of a concrete convention hall.

item.title: Curve balls: Making the Esports World Cup production run smoothly
item.description: SVG Europe - Gravity Media on what goes wrong and gets fixed: a last-minute location change, a late call to add cinema cameras on the main stage, four stages. Useful for the 'how plans change' side.

item.title: Ingesting Live Video Streams at Global Scale
item.description: Twitch Engineering - Twitch's video ingest team on points of presence, backbone and origin data centers. Software side of getting a live stream to viewers. Read it for the pipeline, not the stage.

item.title: [recommended] Live from the Esports World Cup: Inside the production gallery
item.description: SVG Europe - Gallery-level detail: the TD's switcher setup, ATEMs for extra language and sponsor streams, 110 encoders sending about 280 streams, 10-12 live hours per stage per day.

item.title: [recommended] On the job with IATSE Local 28
item.description: Don McIntosh (NW Labor Press) - Reported day on a KISS arena build with local riggers, explaining the team above and below the deck and how touring and house crews work together.

item.title: 1,000 crew, 270 gaming PCs, 9 miles of fiber: Behind the scenes at IEM Katowice
item.description: The Next Web - ESL's IEM Katowice from a visitor's tour: the internet link feeding concurrent matches on four stages to the cloud. Dated (2017) and light, but shows the LAN-event backbone.

item.title: [recommended] Labor of love: rigger
item.description: Ben Mazuer interview (Petzl) - A working rigger talks through long setup-and-strike days, ceiling load limits, team rotation, fatigue and getting started locally.

item.title: 7 Days, Zero Sleep, Millimetric Passion: Behind the Scenes of the PMGC World Finals
item.description: Sahneva Editorial Team - A PUBG Mobile vendor account focuses on physical stage panels, LED fit, overhead rigging and cross-language coordination at the 2023 Istanbul final.

item.title: The largest VALORANT production to date and how cloud computing enabled it
item.description: Mad City - Fully distributed production crew (TD, audio, replay, graphics, observers) working from a cloud studio. Early example of the remote model Riot now runs permanently.

item.title: EVO Championship - Mastering eSports Production
item.description: Trust Fall Technology Group - An Evo vendor case study explains nine stage builds, concurrent load-ins, 3D visualization, pre-rigging and advance programming.

item.title: The Team Behind Worlds 2022 Esports Broadcast
item.description: Riot Games - Who actually staffs Worlds: people from film, TV, sports, music and live entertainment. Good for seeing what roles exist and where PA-type people come from.

item.title: [recommended] Before Doors
item.description: hob.farm - A Las Vegas house-crew account of a five-hour concert load-in after both loading elevators failed.

item.title: [recommended] Esports World Cup 2025: Inside EFG's Hybrid Production
item.description: Sports Video Group - ESL FACEIT Group's head of broadcast engineering on running multiple stages, studios and server rooms across several buildings, mixing baseband and ST 2110.

item.title: [recommended] How Riot Esports Delivers Worlds 2022 Broadcast to a Global Audience
item.description: Riot Games - The 'world feed' model: Riot builds a kit of venue footage, graphics and music, and 22 partners make 21 language shows from it. Also covers how a broadcast day starts with a story meeting days before going live.

item.title: [recommended] Let's Load in!
item.description: SoundGirls (byline not exposed in fetched article) - A touring audio lead walks through Mean Girls load-in, from truck order and cable runs to splitting the local crew and tuning the room.

item.title: How Riot used tech from The Mandalorian to build Worlds' mixed reality stage
item.description: The Verge - LED volume stage for the 2020 Shanghai Worlds, built on a compressed schedule when travel stopped. Older and consumer-press level, but a clear picture of stage tech.
